name: Veg Biryani
blurb: Basmati layered with vegetables, saffron and fried onions, cooked sealed.

steps.text: Soak the rice for 30 minutes and the saffron in the warm milk.
Cook the vegetables in ghee with ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, yogurt, mint and salt until half done.
Boil the rice with the whole spices, bay leaves and salt until 70% done. Drain.
Layer the rice over the vegetables. Top with saffron milk, fried onions and a little ghee.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat.

name: Matar Paneer
blurb: Paneer and peas in a tomato and onion gravy. The weeknight favourite.

steps.text: Fry the cumin, then the onions until golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add the peas, a cup of water and salt and simmer.
Add the paneer, kasuri methi and garam masala. Simmer three minutes and add coriander.

name: Lemon Rice
blurb: Rice with lemon, turmeric and a crunchy tempering of dals and peanuts. Lunchbox food.

steps.text: Cook the rice and spread it out to cool.
Fry the peanuts, dals, mustard seeds, red chillies, green chillies, ginger and curry leaves in oil.
Add hing and turmeric, take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice and salt.
Fold in the rice gently.

name: Masala Omelette
blurb: A thin omelette with onion, chilli and coriander, the Indian way.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the chopped vegetables, spices and salt.
Pour into a hot buttered pan and spread thin.
Cook until set underneath, fold and cook a minute more.

name: Egg Bhurji
blurb: Spiced scrambled eggs with onion, tomato and chilli. With pav or toast.

steps.text: Fry the cumin in butter, then the onion and chilli until soft.
Add the tomato and spices and cook until soft.
Pour in the beaten eggs with salt and stir on low heat until just set.
Add coriander.

name: Coconut Ladoo
blurb: Coconut and condensed milk rolled into balls. Ten minutes, no fuss.

steps.text: Toast the coconut in ghee for two minutes.
Add the condensed milk and cardamom and stir until it comes together.
Cool a little and roll into balls with a cashew in each.

name: Masala Chaas
blurb: Spiced buttermilk with roasted cumin, ginger and coriander. After every Gujarati meal.

steps.text: Blend the yogurt with 3 cups of cold water, ginger, chilli, coriander and mint.
Stir in the cumin, kala namak, chaat masala and salt. Serve cold.

name: Pindi Chole
blurb: Dark, dry chickpeas cooked with tea, finished with sizzling ghee and ginger.

steps.text: Soak the chana overnight. Pressure cook with the tea tied in a cloth, the cardamom, bay leaves and salt until soft.
Drain, keeping a little water. Toss the chana with chole masala, anardana and amchur.
Heat the ghee with cumin, ginger strips and slit chillies until sizzling and pour over.
Cover, simmer ten minutes and serve with sliced onion.

name: Gobi Paratha
blurb: Flatbread stuffed with grated cauliflower and spices. Butter on top.

steps.text: Knead the atta with salt and water into a soft dough. Rest it.
Grate the cauliflower, salt it and squeeze out the water after 10 minutes.
Mix with ginger, chillies, coriander, ajwain, chilli powder, garam masala and amchur.
Stuff, roll and cook on a hot tawa with ghee until golden on both sides.

name: Moong Dal Chilla
blurb: Yellow moong dal pancakes with ginger and onion. Quick and filling.

steps.text: Soak the dal for 3 hours.
Grind with ginger, chillies, cumin, hing, turmeric and salt to a smooth batter.
Stir in the onion and coriander.
Spread on a hot pan, drizzle oil and cook both sides until golden.

name: Hyderabadi Haleem
blurb: Wheat, lentils and mutton cooked for hours and beaten smooth. The Ramzan dish.

steps.text: Soak the wheat and dals for 6 hours.
Cook the mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli, turmeric, whole spices and water until it falls apart.
Cook the wheat and dals in water until very soft.
Shred the mutton, add the wheat and dals and beat with a wooden masher until smooth and stretchy.
Finish with garam masala, ghee, fried onions, mint and lemon.

name: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
blurb: Baby potatoes in a red yogurt gravy with fennel and dry ginger. No onion, no garlic.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes until just done, peel and prick them all over.
Fry them in mustard oil until golden. Set aside.
In the same oil add the hing, whole spices and the chilli powder mixed with a little water.
Whisk in the yogurt with fennel and dry ginger, stirring until it boils.
Add the potatoes and a cup of water. Cover and cook on low until the gravy is thick.

name: Chicken Ghee Roast
blurb: Mangalore’s fiery red chicken, roasted in ghee until it clings.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken with yogurt, turmeric, lemon and salt for 30 minutes.
Roast the chillies, coriander, cumin, pepper and fenugreek in a little ghee. Grind with garlic, tamarind and water to a paste.
Cook the chicken in a spoon of ghee until nearly done. Set aside.
Fry the paste in the rest of the ghee until it darkens and the ghee separates.
Add the chicken, jaggery and curry leaves and roast until coated and dry.

name: Kosha Mangsho
blurb: Mutton slow-cooked in its own masala until dark and clinging. Bengal’s Sunday lunch.

steps.text: Marinate the mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder and salt for an hour.
Heat the mustard oil until it smokes. Add the sugar, bay leaves and whole spices, then the sliced onions, and fry deep brown.
Add the mutton and potatoes. Cook on medium, stirring often, until the oil separates.
Add the cumin and a little water at a time. Cover and cook until the mutton is tender and the masala dark.
Sprinkle garam masala and rest five minutes.

name: Shorshe Maach
blurb: Fish in a sharp mustard sauce with green chillies. Eat it with plain rice.

steps.text: Soak the mustard seeds in warm water for 15 minutes, then grind with 2 green chillies, a pinch of salt and a little water.
Rub the fish with turmeric and salt and fry lightly in mustard oil. Set aside.
In the same oil splutter the kalonji and slit chillies. Add the mustard paste, turmeric and a cup of water.
Slide in the fish and simmer gently until cooked.

name: Chingri Malai Curry
blurb: Prawns in a mild coconut milk gravy with whole spices.

steps.text: Rub the prawns with turmeric and salt and sear them in hot oil for a minute. Set aside.
Fry the bay leaves and whole spices, then the grated onion and ginger until soft.
Add the chilli powder and a splash of water, then the coconut milk, sugar and slit chillies.
Add the prawns and simmer until just cooked. Finish with garam masala and a spoon of ghee.

name: Chicken Xacuti
blurb: Chicken in a dark curry of roasted coconut, poppy seeds and whole spices.

steps.text: Dry roast the coconut until deep brown. Set aside.
Roast the chillies, coriander, cumin, poppy seeds and whole garam masala until fragrant.
Grind the coconut and spices with garlic, ginger and a little water to a smooth paste.
Fry the sliced onions in oil until golden. Add the chicken, turmeric and salt and sear.
Add the paste and a cup of water. Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon.

name: Pork Vindaloo
blurb: Pork in a hot, sharp sauce of chilli, vinegar and garlic. Better the next day.

steps.text: Soak the chillies in the vinegar for 20 minutes.
Grind them with the vinegar, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, whole garam masala and turmeric to a paste.
Rub the pork with the paste and salt. Rest it, overnight if you can.
Fry the onions in oil until brown, add the pork and its marinade and sear.
Add a cup of water and the jaggery. Cover and cook slowly until the pork is soft.

name: Lucknowi Biryani
blurb: Mutton and rice cooked dum, perfumed with kewra and saffron. Gentler than Hyderabad’s.

steps.text: Marinate the mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, half the fried onions and salt.
Cook the mutton in ghee with the whole spices until tender, adding water as needed. Leave a little gravy.
Boil the soaked rice with cardamom and salt until 70% done. Drain.
Layer the rice over the mutton. Top with saffron milk, kewra, fried onions and ghee.
Seal and cook on the lowest heat.

name: Nihari
blurb: Slow-cooked mutton stew, thick and peppery, eaten at dawn in old Lucknow and Delhi.

steps.text: Fry the sliced onions in ghee until golden. Keep half for the top.
Add the mutton and ginger-garlic paste and sear well.
Add the nihari masala, chilli, fennel and dry ginger, then 6 cups of water. Cover and cook very slowly.
Whisk the atta into a little water, stir it in and simmer until the stew thickens.
Serve with the fried onions, ginger strips and lemon.
